steps.title: Five key reds
steps.body: The Douro allows over 100 grapes, but five are recommended for quality. Touriga Nacional: floral, dark, structured. Touriga Franca, the most planted: perfumed, elegant. Tinta Roriz, Tempranillo: red fruit and body. Tinta Barroca: soft, sweet fruit, early ripening. Tinto Cão: acidity and finesse, low yields.

steps.title: Field blends
steps.body: Many old Douro vineyards are field blends, vinhas velhas, with dozens of grapes planted together, often over 80 years old. They're picked and fermented together, giving complexity. Whites, from Rabigato, Viosinho, Gouveio and Códega do Larinho, grow at higher, cooler sites and make dry whites and white Port.

steps.prompt: Match each grape to its role.
steps.explanation: Douro blends draw on many natives.

steps.body: Vinhas velhas, old vines, on a Douro label often means a field blend of many grapes, a living record of how the region was planted.

steps.prompt: Which is the Douro's most planted grape?
steps.explanation: Touriga Franca covers the most area.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Five recommended reds lead, from Touriga Nacional to Tinto Cão
Touriga Franca is the most planted
